web_evidence.title: A Gentleman in Moscow: Questions For Consideration
web_evidence.note: Towles’s official reader’s guide states that most of the novel is third person from the Count’s viewpoint and describes the separate overarching narrator in footnotes, Addendums, and historical introductions.

web_evidence.title: A Gentleman in Moscow Reader’s Guide
web_evidence.note: The publisher’s guide independently describes the majority as third-person narration focused on the Count and identifies the overarching narrator as a distinct narrating perspective.

web_evidence.title: Amor Towles on A Gentleman in Moscow and the Writer's Craft
web_evidence.note: In a direct interview, Towles says roughly 90 percent is told in third person and explains that a second narrator supplies footnotes, Addendums, and historical introductions; neither narrator participates as a story character.

web_evidence.title: A Gentleman in Moscow by Amor Towles — Excerpt
web_evidence.note: A seven-page copyrighted interior excerpt sustains external third-person narration of the Count and Nina, including the Count’s perceptions and actions.

web_evidence.title: Narrating Russia: History, Class, and Cultural Identity in Amor Towles’s A Gentleman in Moscow
web_evidence.note: A peer-reviewed literary article analyzes the novel as third-person narration following the Count for most of the story, supplemented by an omniscient narrator and historical sections.

person_note: The Goodreads material repeatedly shows the Count narrated externally in third person, often through free-indirect access to his thoughts. First-person forms in the sample are dialogue, embedded thought, or universal/essayistic “we,” not a participating base narrator. Live research resolves the unusual structure: Towles distinguishes a Count-aligned third-person voice from a more historically informed overarching voice appearing in footnotes, Addendums, and dated introductions. These are two nonparticipating narratorial voices, not sustained sections in different grammatical persons, so the book is THIRD rather than ALTERNATING. The main residual uncertainty is that some clipped quotes cannot identify person independently, but the authorized interior excerpt and multiple whole-book structural sources remove meaningful book-level doubt.
